αὐτοὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)

αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv.

γέροντα: γέρων — old man, elder; masc. acc. sg.

εὐνήν: εὐνή — bed, bedding, marriage-bed; fem. acc. sg.

θείοιο: θεῖος — divine, godlike; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)

κακόν: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. sg.: ’a bad thing, evil’

κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κελεύθου: κέλευθος — way, road, journey, voyage; gen. sg.

λίην: λίαν — very much, exceedingly; adv., Ionic λίην (= Attic λίαν)
λιγὺς: λιγύς — clear-sounding, shrill, whistling; masc. nom. sg., usually of voices/instruments but here of wind (λιγὺς οὖρος ’a clear, keen wind’)
λόχον: λόχος — ambush, body of men lying in wait; masc. acc. sg. (of the men hidden inside the wooden horse)

μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.

μέγ: μέγας — great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, elided (μέγ’ = μέγα): ’greatly’
μέλαν: μέλας — black, dark; neut. nom./acc. sg.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’)

μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ)
μεγάροισι: μέγαρον — hall; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
μελέτω: μέλω — be a care, be a concern; pres. imper. 3 sg. impersonal: ’let it be a care’
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μευ: ἐγώ — I; encl. gen. sg., epic μευ (= Attic μου): ’of me’, with κλύω ’hear me’
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
νέεσθαι: νέομαι — go, return home; pres. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic νεῖσθαι)
νηυσὶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νηυσί(ν)
νηῦς: ναῦς — ship; nom. sg., epic νηῦς
νυ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νόσφιν: νόσφιν — apart, far off, away; adv.
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’
ξανθὸς: ξανθός — fair-haired, yellow, tawny; masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Menelaus
ξεῖνε: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); voc. sg.
οἰχομένοιο: οἴχομαι — be gone, have gone away; pres. part. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), perfect sense: ’gone’

οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.

οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even

οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)

προπάροιθε: προπάροιθε — before, in front of; adv./prep. + gen.
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’

πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πόντῳ: πόντος — sea, open sea; dat. sg.
πόποι: πόποι — (in ὢ πόποι) exclamation of surprise or displeasure: ’ah! well!’; origin unknown
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.

σπέσσι: σπέος — cave; neut. dat. pl. (plural for a single cave), epic -εσσι

τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τρεῖς: τρεῖς — three; numeral, masc./fem. nom. pl.

ἀμειβόμενος: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. masc. nom. sg. mid.
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv.

ἐὺ: ἐΰ — well (Attic εὖ, printed without a diaeresis); adv.
ἐὼν: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ὤν)

ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.

ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.

ἔχειν: ἔχω — have, hold, keep; pres. inf.

ἠριγένεια: ἠριγένεια — early-born; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἤια: ἤια — provisions for a journey; neut. acc. pl.
ἤλυθεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; epic aor. 3 sg. (= Attic ἦλθεν): ’came’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥρως: ἥρως — hero, man of standing; masc. nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἦε: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ), spelled ἦε in ἦε καὶ οὐκί ’or not’
ἦμος: ἦμος — when, at the time when; temporal conj.
ἰχθυόεντα: ἰχθυόεις — fish-filled, teeming with fish; neut. acc. pl. (ἰχθυόεντα κέλευθα ’fish-filled paths’, of the sea)
ἴσασιν: οἶδα — know; perf. 3 pl. (pres. force), ν-movable: ’they know’
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀχθήσας: ὀχθέω — be vexed, be troubled; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’vexed, troubled’
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁμιλήσειεν: ὁμιλέω — be in company with, meet, consort with; aor. opt. 3 sg., wish: ’might he come among’
ὅθεν: ὅθεν — from where, whence; relative adv.
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅσσ: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος, double σ) — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσσ’ = ὅσσα): ’as much as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’)
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι)
ὑμῖν: σύ (pl. ὑμεῖς) — you; dat. pl.: ’to you’
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’)
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
ὕπο: ὑπό — under, in; postpositive prep. + dat., anastrophe (ὕπνῳ ὕπο = ὑπὸ ὕπνῳ): ’in (sweet sleep)’
ὠκύμοροί: ὠκύμορος — swift-doomed, early-doomed (ὠκύς + μόρος); masc. nom. pl.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’)
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
ῥοδοδάκτυλος: ῥοδοδάκτυλος — rose-fingered; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
